children: Albany International shares rose after its Albany Engineered Composites segment said it reached an agreement with Boeing to continue composite fuselage frame manufacturing for the 787 Dreamliner.
The stock was 6% higher, at $62.27, in midday trading, and is 23% higher year-to-date.

Albany said that under the agreement, it will continue to manufacture about 300 unique composite fuselage frames for the 787 Dreamliner, including forward sections 41 and 43 and aft section 47. Albany has produced composite fuselage frames for sections 41 and 43 since Boeing's original award in 2014.
The Boeing 787 work is performed at Albany's facility in Salt Lake City, Utah.
Baird raised their price target for Albany International to $75 a share from $64 a share, while maintaining a neutral rating on the stock.
